correctness.rationale: For each bit the Fourier sum factors into a three-term dyadic root-of-unity sum. Concavity of \(2\cos(\pi t)-1\) on [0,1/2] and 3 not dividing any dyadic denominator prove every factor has modulus at least the reciprocal of its order, hence the product is at least \(2^{-n(n+1)/2}\). A single explicit pair of frequencies approximating the two primitive cube roots at all scales gives the matching upper bound \((4\pi/3)^n2^{-n(n+1)/2}\). The spectral condition number and limit follow from diagonalization, maximum \(3^n\), and the two-sided bounds. A finite standalone checker verifies direct versus factored sums for 1364 Fourier positions at lengths 1 through 5 and witnesses through 10. Floating point finite checks are not mistaken for all-length proof.

originality.rationale: The central novelty assertion is the sharp quadratic coefficient of the logarithmic spectral condition number, not qualitative zero-freeness. The 1995 Lam-Leung theorem combined with the digit factorization already implies no Fourier zeros, and this implication is explicitly credited. Its stated weight-set result does not provide the simultaneous-scale lower/upper modulus estimates. The inspected Pascal-row source addresses different invariants; bounded searches found no equivalent quantitative two-dimensional dyadic no-carry condition-number theorem. Residual risk of prior cyclotomic-product bounds is documented.
residual_risks: Specialized cyclotomic products, digital Fourier Riesz products, or discrete Sierpiński spectra may contain an equivalent quantitative least-modulus estimate in sources not retrieved or not inspected in full.
The finite checker is not an independent proof; independent validation remains outstanding.

value.rationale: The no-carry indicator is the natural Sierpiński/Pascal odd-entry pattern on a finite dyadic torus. Its Fourier convolution is always invertible, but the sharp leading logarithmic condition-number coefficient is \(n^2/2\), an extreme form of stability loss not implied by standard binary counts or qualitative nonvanishing. This structural scale matching is informative for deconvolution on digital fractal approximants; no false promise of exact finite-n extremizers is made.
